transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because my sleep is just all broken up now. I get off my overnight shift and... I just still lie there wide awake. And then, when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared. It just feels like I never rested at all.

When you wake up scared in the middle of the night, can you describe what you're experiencing—are you having bad dreams that you remember, or does the fear just suddenly hit you without any dream content?

I don't really know, honestly. I just... I wake up and my heart is pounding. I can't really remember if I was dreaming about something bad. It's just this sudden feeling of being terrified, like something is wrong, but I don't know what.
When you wake up terrified with your heart pounding, do these episodes happen at roughly the same time each night, or do they seem to happen randomly throughout the night?

It seems pretty random. Like I said, my sleep is just totally broken up right now. I get off my overnight shift and just lie there wide awake for a long time. So whenever I finally do manage to drift off—no matter what time it is—that's when I wake up scared like that. I just never feel like I actually rested.
How long has this problem with waking up scared been going on—did it start right when you began working the overnight shift, or did it develop sometime after you started that schedule?

It's been happening for about a year and two months now. It started right around the time my agency switched me to these rotating overnight shifts... and they gave me a bunch of extra paperwork to do, too. So yeah, it's been going on since then.

You mentioned the shift change and extra paperwork started around the same time—did anything else happen about a year and two months ago that was particularly stressful or upsetting? Like a major life event or something disturbing that you experienced?

No, not really. I mean, the schedule change and the extra work were stressful enough on their own. But as far as like... a major life event or something really disturbing happening back then? No, nothing like that. It was just the job stuff.

On the nights when you wake up terrified with your heart pounding, have you ever been able to remember any actual nightmare or bad dream—like a specific scary scenario or image—or is it always just the fear and physical symptoms without any dream you can recall?

No, I never really remember any actual dreams. It's just... I wake up and my heart is going crazy, and I'm just terrified. But there's no picture in my head or a specific nightmare that I can recall. It's always just that awful feeling of being scared without knowing why.
